translations.title: Why should protective falling separate the takeover trigger from post-takeover damage mitigation?
translations.answer: SafeFall separates a proprioceptive GRU unavoidable-fall trigger from a damage-aware protective policy: normal locomotion remains unchanged until recovery is judged impossible. Engineering acceptance must independently validate false-alarm rate/lead time and contact/reaction-force/torque metrics. The paper's G1 and near-flat results do not replace target-robot hard limits, an external supervisor, and staged impact testing.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The fall predictor is revalidated for the active nominal policy, payload, firmware, and terrain.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Component vulnerability weights and hard limits are rebuilt for the target robot.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Flat or near-flat humanoid locomotion falls inside the validated disturbance distribution
translations.applicability.robots.0: Unitree G1 in the paper; any other robot requires new data, rewards, limits, and staged validation
translations.applicability.simulators.0: Contact simulator with independently checked collision geometry, solver, and damage proxies
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper provides predictor ablations, more than 5,000 simulated falls, metric-specific baselines, and G1 impulse experiments. Confidence is deliberately lower because official code/raw trials are unavailable, flat-terrain scope is explicit, collision proxies are simulator-dependent, and the predictor requires retraining across nominal policies.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Figure 2; Tables II-V; Figures 5-6; Section V limitations
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines the predictor/takeover/protector split, reports FAR/lead-time and simulated damage metrics, gives G1 impulse evidence, and states terrain/compute limitations.
translations.evidence.0.title: SafeFall: Learning Protective Control for Humanoid Robots
translations.safety.command_limits: Use robot-specific joint, velocity, current, torque, contact, and impact limits that cannot be traded against the learned reward.
translations.safety.emergency_stop: Provide an independent hardware emergency stop and deterministic fallback for predictor timeout, score chatter, invalid actions, or communication loss.
translations.safety.protective_controls: Start with suspension or soft capture, low-energy perturbations, protected components, and automatic aborts before expanding direction, speed, or fall height.
translations.safety.robot_specific_warning: Paper percentages and G1 vulnerability weights are not transferable command limits or a permission to fall another robot.
translations.safety.staged_deployment: Validate labels and false-alarm rate/lead time offline, then simulation damage metrics, low-energy tethered hardware, direction/speed matrices, and only then bounded untethered trials with inspection after every impact.
translations.terms.1: Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU, 门控循环单元)
